subject: Synchronized multi-year renewal + staged capacity ramp for Acme Retail
messages:
From: Ellen Price <ellen.price@acmeretail.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-02T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal alignment across U.S. + EMEA and staged capacity request

Jonas —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We wanted to start a thread to formalize what Acme needs for the upcoming renewal (contracts for both the US and EMEA subsidiaries). High level: we want a single co-term agreement with a 36‑month base term, but with a staged capacity ramp tied to usage so we don't overcommit up front. Key asks from our side: 

- Co-terming across legal entities (US + EMEA) with one Master SOW and regional addenda.
- Staged capacity unlocks (quarterly triggers tied to monthly token/embedding consumption).
- Annual true-up (or burn-credit) mechanism.
- Clear auto-renew opt-out window and notice periods.
- Procurement timeline: budget sign-off by Oct 31, preferred signature before EOY.

Can you send a proposed structure and draft SOW we can circulate with Procurement and Legal? Also please include a sample pricing cadence (how credits/billing move as we scale).

- Ellen
VP, Platform Partnerships
Acme Retail

Attachments: none in this note
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Ellen Price <ellen.price@acmeretail.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal alignment across U.S. + EMEA and staged capacity request

Ellen, thank you — this aligns with what we discussed. I attached a working SOW (SOW_v3.pdf) that maps to the structure below; happy to walk through on a quick call. Proposed high-level approach: 

1) Term & co-terming: 36 months co-term, single MSA with regional addenda called out.
2) Staged capacity ramp: baseline committed capacity (monthly token equivalent) with quarterly unlocks at 25% increments when trailing 30‑day usage >= trigger threshold.
3) Canary period: first 90 days after go-live allow for a measured burst with rollback protection and a one-time onboarding credit.
4) Financial controls: quarterly true-up and annual reconciliation; prepay credit options available if they want predictable unit economics.
5) Auto-renew: default auto-renew with a 60‑day opt-out window (we can flip to manual-only if Procurement requires).

If OK, can we target an internal alignment call Tuesday Oct 5 (I looped Camila who will own the pricing cadence)? After that we'll incorporate Procurement's redlines.

Attachments: SOW_v3.pdf (pdf, 324KB)

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-03T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: pricing + ramp mechanics for Acme (notes)

Team —
Recap from today's pricing brainstorm (bullet form so we can drop into the SOW):

- Baseline commit = X token-equivalent (TE). Quarterly unlocks of 25% of baseline when trailing 30d usage > 85% of current committed capacity. Unlocks are additive up to a ceiling of 200% of baseline.
- Canary capacity: 30% additional capacity reserved for first 90 days; customer can elect to keep or release (if release, credits applied against next quarter).
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-up with annual reconciliation. If usage exceeds commit, overage billed at overage rate; if under, credits carry forward for 12 months.
- Prepay discount tiers: 5% for annual prepay, 12% for multi-year prepay applied to committed baseline only.
- Auto-renew: default on with 60-day opt-out. Procurement occasionally insists on manual renewal — suggest we offer an exception with a 2% admin fee to offset churn risk.

Open items where we need legal or product input: SLA credit language for regional outages across co-termed entities; exact rollback mechanics for canary. I attached Acme_redlines.docx they sent earlier (redlines are mostly around liability/SLA and the 'auto-bill' language).

Ask: Jonas — can you confirm whether we can flex the prepay discount for 36-month commit (we have room up to 15% if they go full prepay). Kimberly — can you prep sample invoice cadence for US vs EMEA and highlight tax/VAT considerations?

Attachments: Acme_redlines.docx (docx, 48KB)

Thanks,
Camila
Director, Renewal Strategy | Redwood Inference
From: Javier Torres <javier.torres@acmeretail.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Ellen Price <ellen.price@acmeretail.com>, procurement@acmeretail.com
Date: 2026-10-09T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal alignment across U.S. + EMEA and staged capacity request — redlines + timeline

Jonas —

Thanks for the draft SOW. Procurement and Legal reviewed and sent consolidated redlines (attached). High-level asks from Procurement: 

- Confirmed term request: 36 months, co-term across entities, with an annual true-up and an explicit early-exit calculation (penalty schedule).
- Staged unlocks are acceptable but want explicit numeric triggers documented (we proposed monthly consumption thresholds; your 85% threshold looks OK).
- Request an explicit rollback clause for canary capacity and a capped credit for any SLA shortfall.
- Auto-renew must be opt-in for EMEA entity due to local procurement rules (they cannot be auto-renewed without 90 days notice). We're asking for a 90-day opt-out for EMEA and keeping 60-day for US.
- Timeline: final commercial terms by Oct 15, legal review complete by Oct 22, target signature before Oct 31.

We attached our redlines (Acme_redlines.docx) and a procurement timeline spreadsheet (not attached here; will share if needed). Please confirm whether the prepay discounts you mentioned can be applied on a per-entity basis (we may prepay the US but not EMEA). 

-Javier
Head of Procurement, Acme Retail

Attachments: Acme_redlines.docx (docx, 48KB)
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Javier Torres <javier.torres@acmeretail.com>, Ellen Price <ellen.price@acmeretail.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-14T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal alignment across U.S. + EMEA and staged capacity request — proposed final structure

Javier / Ellen —

Thanks for the redlines and clear timeline. Summary of the proposed final structure we can deliver (this will be reflected in SOW_v3 and the updated MSA):

- Term: 36 months co-term (single MSA with US and EMEA addenda).
- Capacity & ramp: baseline committed TE with quarterly staged unlocks at +25% when trailing 30d usage >= 85% of committed capacity. Unlocks are additive up to 200% of baseline.
- Canary: 90-day canary window with a one-time onboarding burst allowance; rollback clause included with credits equal to unused committed capacity during rollback quarter.
- Financials: quarterly true-ups; annual reconciliation. Prepay discounts can be applied per-entity (US prepay allowed with up to 15% discount for full 36-month prepay; EMEA eligible but subject to VAT/tax adjustments).
- Auto-renew: US = 60-day opt-out; EMEA = 90-day opt-out as requested. We'll put a short exception clause that allows Procurement to require manual renewal with a 2% admin fee if they opt out of auto-renew entirely.
- SLA & credits: regional SLA definitions with capped credits; legal to confirm final language, but we will use our standard regional SLA table and include exception handling for cross-region incidents.

Next steps: Camila will incorporate the redlines into SOW_v3 and we will circulate a final SOW + redline replacement for sign-off by Oct 15. Once agreed, we'll send a DocuSign envelope (link below) for both entities.

DocuSign (prelim): https://docusign.com/envelope/12345ABC
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-2026-Q4-RAMP

If there are any last-minute items, flag them today so we can get legal review queued.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
